q: Expander graphs have important connections to information theory. An (n,d,λ)-expander with second largest eigenvalue λ has the mixing time of a random walk on it proportional to:
exp: Mixing time of random walk on an expander: tmix ≈ log n / log(d/λ). The spectral gap d−λ controls the exponential convergence rate; mixing time is O(log n / spectral_gap). Expanders are crucial for derandomization (converting random walks to pseudorandom walks).
